sents.text: Welcome to Course zero, the prep course.
Before we train a single model, we learn the ground every AI tool stands on, and it starts with Linux.
In this lesson: what Linux is, why almost all AI runs on it, and how to open a Linux terminal in two minutes, for free.
Linux is an operating system, like Windows or macOS: the layer that runs a computer's hardware and its programs.
It's free and open source, which means anyone can use it, read its code and change it.
You may never have seen it, but you use it every day: it runs most of the web's servers, and Android is built on it.
Now here's why it matters for AI.
When you train a model in the cloud, rent a GPU machine, or run a notebook in Colab, the computer underneath is almost always Linux.
For years now, every one of the world's five hundred fastest supercomputers has run Linux.
So the instructions you'll meet in tutorials, papers and real jobs are written for Linux.
It costs nothing, so it can run on thousands of machines at once.
It was built for servers, so it works well with no screen at all.
GPU and AI tools are built and tested for it.
And everything in Linux can be done by typing commands, which means it can be written into scripts and repeated exactly.
